definitions.explanation: The polite form of {餅|もち} (mochi), a traditional Japanese food made from glutinous rice that has been pounded into a sticky, chewy mass. A staple of New Year celebrations and used in many traditional sweets and dishes.

examples.japanese: お{正月|しょうがつ}にお{餅|もち}を{食|た}べる。
examples.english: To eat mochi at New Year's.

examples.japanese: お{餅|もち}を{焼|や}いて{醤油|しょうゆ}をつけた。
examples.english: I grilled the mochi and dipped it in soy sauce.

examples.japanese: {毎年|まいとし}お{正月|しょうがつ}になると、お{餅|もち}を{喉|のど}に{詰|つ}まらせる{事故|じこ}のニュースが{報道|ほうどう}される。
examples.english: Every New Year, there are news reports about accidents where people choke on mochi.

examples.japanese: おばあちゃんが{臼|うす}と{杵|きね}でお{餅|もち}をついてくれた。
examples.english: Grandma pounded mochi for us with a mortar and pestle.

notes:
The polite お prefix is standard with {餅|もち} in everyday speech, making お{餅|もち} the default conversational form. The お is not merely decorative; dropping it can sound curt in casual conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{餅|もち}をつく: to pound mochi
- お{餅|もち}を{焼|や}く: to grill/toast mochi
- お{餅|もち}を{煮|に}る: to boil mochi (in soup)
- {切|き}り{餅|もち}: pre-cut mochi blocks (sold in packages)
- {丸|まる}{餅|もち}: round mochi (Kansai style)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Mochi is deeply associated with {正月|しょうがつ} (New Year). It appears in {雑煮|ぞうに} (New Year's soup), {鏡餅|かがみもち} (decorative stacked mochi), and {磯辺焼|いそべや}き (grilled mochi wrapped in nori). The shape varies by region: round in western Japan, rectangular in eastern Japan. Every January, Japanese media report on choking incidents ({窒息|ちっそく}{事故|じこ}) among elderly people, making mochi safety a recurring seasonal topic.

RELATED WORDS:
- {餅|もち}: mochi — the base form, used in compounds
- {大福|だいふく}: daifuku — mochi stuffed with sweet bean paste
- {草餅|くさもち}: mugwort mochi — green mochi flavored with yomogi
- {白玉|しらたま}: shiratama — small mochi dumplings made from rice flour
